objective:
Audit the Tombola draw contracts in this repository: src/TombolaDraw.sol and src/TombolaSplitter.sol are the new code and the focus; src/DrandBeacon.sol (drand evmnet BLS verification on BN254, via the vendored randa-mu library under vendor/bls-solidity) is reused from an earlier, already reviewed design and is in scope only as the dependency the draw relies on. Solidity 0.8.26, via_ir, cancun. README.md and DESIGN.md describe the system; test/TombolaDraw.t.sol has 19 passing tests including a real evmnet round from test/fixtures/evmnet.json.

System. Tombola is a lottery token launched on Pons V2 (Robinhood Chain). Pons charges a creator tax on every trade and accrues it in ETH in its fee escrow for the creatorFeeRecipient, which is TombolaSplitter. Anyone calls TombolaSplitter.harvest(): it claims the escrow and splits the ETH 7333 / 2000 / 667 bps between TombolaDraw.fundRegular(), TombolaDraw.fundMega() and a plain send to the team fee wallet (rounding dust to the team). TombolaDraw holds the two pots and the draw ledger. A keeper (hot wallet, immutable address) calls commit(track, snapshotTime, drandRound, amount): it reserves amount from the track's pot and commits to a FUTURE drand round (beacon.roundTime(round) >= snapshotTime + 10 minutes, round not yet proven on chain, snapshotTime <= block.timestamp, one open draw per track). Off chain the keeper rebuilds the eligibility list from the token's Transfer logs at the snapshot block (weightFor: balance >= 10,000e18, held 30 minutes, 1x to 3x over 72 h), publishes it, and calls settle(id, drandSignature, root, totalWeight, winner, cumulativeBefore, weight, proof): the beacon verifies the BLS signature and stores keccak256(signature); randomWord = keccak256(abi.encode(randomness, id)); the leaf keccak256(bytes.concat(keccak256(abi.encode(winner, cumulativeBefore, weight)))) must verify against root (sorted-pair Merkle); weight > 0 and cumulativeBefore + weight <= totalWeight; randomWord % totalWeight must fall in [cumulativeBefore, cumulativeBefore + weight). The prize is sent with a 50,000 gas stipend; a failed send is credited to unclaimed[winner] and claim(to) pays it later. rollover(id, signature, root) returns the prize to the pot when nobody was eligible. A guardian (cold wallet) may cancel(id) a committed, unsettled draw; after 7 days past the round's time anyone may. solvent() states the invariant balance >= potRegular + potMega + reserved + unclaimedTotal.

Trust model, so findings are ranked against it. The contracts are meant to enforce: (1) the drand round was committed before anyone could know it; (2) the randomness is drand's and the winner index is randomWord mod totalWeight over the pinned list; (3) the winner is in the pinned list with the claimed weight and the index falls in its range; (4) ETH only leaves as a settled prize to the proven winner, the team's share from the splitter, or back into a pot on rollover/cancel. The keeper IS trusted to build an honest, complete list with honest weights: that is verified off chain from public data, not by the contract, and is NOT a finding. The keeper choosing when to commit (and so which future round) is accepted. No owner, no upgrade, no withdraw exists by design.

Please focus on: (a) pot solvency and accounting: potRegular / potMega / reserved / unclaimedTotal across commit, settle, rollover, cancel, claim, fundRegular/fundMega/receive, including uint128 amount truncation in commit and any path that breaks solvent(); (b) the commit-before-randomness guarantee: can the keeper or anyone commit to a round whose signature is already public or predictable (COMMIT_DELAY vs drand's 3 s period and clock skew, roundTime arithmetic, the randomness(round) != 0 check, snapshotTime far in the past), and whether settle/rollover could use a different round than committed; (c) the Merkle leaf and winner-range checks: leaf encoding collisions, a proof for a leaf that is not a leaf (intermediate node, duplicated last leaf padding), root == 0, totalWeight inconsistent with the tree, overlapping or gapped cumulative ranges letting the keeper pick between two winners, weight == 0 leaves; (d) re-entrancy and ordering: nonReentrant on settle/rollover/cancel/claim, _pay before/after state, the 50,000 gas stipend and return bomb, the splitter's harvest re-entering through the escrow or the team wallet, the draw's receive() being called by the splitter during harvest; (e) the guardian / cancel / abandon paths: can the guardian or the 7-day anyone-cancel be used to grief a settled or settlable draw, re-cancel, double-return, or lock a track (activeDraw) permanently; what happens with guardian == address(0); (f) griefing: dust amounts, failed sends to the team wallet reverting harvest, a winner contract that reverts, claim(to) by third parties, pots stuck forever, a keeper that never settles; (g) anything that lets the keeper, the guardian, the splitter, the team wallet or any third party take ETH that is not a settled prize or the team's bps share, or move ETH between pots. Also note any mismatch between what the README/DESIGN claim the contract enforces and what the code enforces.

For each finding give the location, the concrete sequence of calls, and the impact in ETH terms; a Foundry reproduction against test/TombolaDraw.t.sol's setUp is welcome. Please classify what is informational (accepted trust in the keeper) separately from what is exploitable.
